structure.overview: The case concerns a judicial review by TPG Technology Consulting Ltd. (Applicant) challenging the disclosure of certain information by the Government of Canada (Respondent) under the Access to Information Act (ATIA). The court partially upheld the Applicant's claims, finding some pricing references and subcontractor profiles exempt from disclosure under ATIA sections 20(1)(b) and (c), but rejected exemptions for other subcontractor information under section 20(1)(d). The judicial review was allowed in part, with costs awarded to the Applicant.

summaries.summary: ATIA balances transparency with protecting confidential, commercial, or proprietary information through exemptions in sections 16 to 21.

citations.why: Shows exemptions balancing disclosure and confidentiality

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Subsection 20(1) of ATIA exempts government institutions from disclosing certain third-party information, specifically paragraphs 20(1)(b), (c), and (d).

citations.why: Identifies relevant exemption provisions

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Paragraph 20(1)(b) requires refusal to disclose confidential financial, commercial, scientific, or technical information supplied by a third party.

citations.why: Defines refusal to disclose confidential third-party info

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Paragraph 20(1)(c) prohibits disclosure if it would likely harm a third party's competitive position or cause financial loss or gain.

citations.why: Defines harm-based disclosure exemption

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Paragraph 20(1)(d) prevents disclosure that could interfere with a third party's contractual or other negotiations.

citations.why: Defines exemption to protect negotiations

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Government institutions must notify third parties and allow submissions before disclosing records containing third-party information.

citations.why: Requires notice and submissions before disclosure

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Third parties can apply for judicial review if the government discloses information against their submissions under ATIA s 44(1).

citations.why: Allows judicial review of disclosure decisions

summaries.summary: The Applicant sent a redacted record version claiming exemptions under ATIA paragraphs 20(1)(b), (c), and (d).

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: PSPC responded that only some information would be redacted, attaching a revised record with planned redactions.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Applicant filed judicial review challenging PSPC's decision to disclose confidential and competitively sensitive information.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court reviews de novo under ATIA s 44(1), deciding whether the information should be disclosed, citing Vavilov, Preventous, and Perreault.

Court's role is to decide disclosure anew

citations.cite: Canada (Health) v Preventous Collaborative Health, 2022 FCA 153 at paras 14-15

citations.cite: Perreault v Canada (Foreign Affairs), 2023 FC 1051 at paras 20, 29
citations.why: Court decides what decision it would have made on disclosure
